speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have right groin pain and abnormal leg positioning following a rear-end collision. To begin my assessment, please tell me exactly how you were positioned in your vehicle at the time of the crash.

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: That confirms the mechanism of injury involves significant deceleration and potential direct impact to the right thigh. Did the impact force strike the right side of your vehicle, or was the force transmitted primarily through the seat and seatbelt?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated.

speaker: Doctor
text: The positioning of your right leg—shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated—is a classic "squared" position suggesting hip dislocation or fracture. Given your history of a rear-end collision and bilateral knee pain, did you hear a loud "pop" or snap at the moment of impact?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Works as an elementary school teacher. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Posterior Hip Dislocation.

The classic presentation of a shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated leg following a high-energy rear-end collision is pathognomonic for a posterior hip dislocation. I will request immediate orthopedic imaging to confirm the diagnosis and rule out associated femoral neck fractures. REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvis_XRay_AAP, Femur_XRay_AAP.
